I am old now, 71 years. I been doing this 50 years on this same 5 mu. My hands know the land. I will do this year like last year — what works, I keep doing. Change is for young people with money to lose.

For my wheat after the maize comes off in autumn — I plant in October like always. I buy the compound fertilizer in bags, the 15-15-15 kind the shop sells. My neighbor Old Wang uses two bags per mu before planting, I do the same, about 50 kg per mu. Then when the wheat stands up in spring at jointing time, I put urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. My father taught me: hungry wheat is thin wheat. Better to give a little extra than to see empty heads at harvest. I got the well so I water four times — before winter to keep roots safe, then returning-green in spring, jointing, and when the grain is filling. Without water the grain stays small. I spray two times — once for the weeds when wheat is small, once when I see the yellow rust starting or bugs on the leaves.

For maize after wheat in June — no time to plow, I just drill the seed right into the stubble, everybody does it now. Hybrid seed of course, the dealer only sells hybrid, cannot save seed anymore like my father did. Same compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg, then at the big-trumpet stage when the plant is up to my chest I scatter urea 25 kg per mu. Maize is hungry, it grows fast. Water one time if rain is short, maybe two. One spray for the borer in the whorl.

Yield — if the weather is normal like most years, wheat gives me about 450 kg per mu, maize maybe 550 kg per mu. Bad weather year, less. Good year, a bit more. I do not count on good years.
